event_name: Victorian Christmas Candlelight Night at William Root House
blurb: The William Root House does one of the more quietly cool holiday events in the area on December 11th. Candlelit rooms decorated with live greens, fruit, and handmade pieces in full 1860s style, cooking demonstrations, and live music running from 4 to 8 PM. It's low-key in the best way. No massive crowds, no inflatable Santas, just a genuinely atmospheric evening in a historic house that reminds you what the holidays looked like before everything was electric and plastic. Good for a date night, good for empty nesters who want something with actual character. Worth the short drive to Marietta.
scoring_notes: Appeals to the educated, culturally curious segment of the Perimeter audience. Empty nesters and couples without kids will find this more appealing than families with young children, which fits the adult-skewing nature of this newsletter. The 1860s historical angle is genuinely differentiated from generic holiday events.

event_name: Taiwanese Winter Night Market Cooking Workshop
venue: Mise en Place Cooking Studio, Roswell
blurb: Taiwan's night markets are genuinely one of the great food experiences in the world, loud, crowded, smoky, and delicious in a way that's hard to replicate anywhere else. This workshop at Mise en Place Cooking Studio tries to bring that energy into a hands-on format on December 4th, which makes it a fun Friday night activity with a bit more substance than dinner and a movie. You're in Roswell, which is a quick shot up 400 from the Perimeter, and it runs 6 to 8:30 so the whole evening is still yours after. Good pick if you like to cook, good pick if you just want to eat well while learning something. Check Mise en Place for ticket pricing and availability.
scoring_notes: High-education, higher-income Perimeter audience maps well to experiential food and cooking events. Friday evening timing is ideal. Roswell is a reasonable distance from the Perimeter area. The Taiwanese night market theme is specific and culturally interesting rather than generic.

blurb: Black Friday night and you're looking for something to do that isn't more shopping. Here's your answer. Fetty Wap is at Coca-Cola Roxy on November 28th, and if you came up listening to Trap Queen on repeat in 2015, this one's going to hit different live. The Battery is an easy night out from the Perimeter, the venue is comfortable, and an 8 PM show means you can eat first without rushing. Grab tickets before they're gone and make it a proper night out.
scoring_notes: Median age of 38 puts this audience squarely in the demographic that knows Fetty Wap's catalog well. Black Friday timing is a genuine differentiator since most people are off work. The Battery location is convenient for Perimeter residents. Adult skew works for this newsletter's audience mix.

blurb: Tyla is one of the most exciting artists to break in the last few years, and Water alone put her on a global stage fast. She's at Coca-Cola Roxy on December 6th, and if you've been sleeping on seeing her live, this is a small enough room that you'll actually feel it rather than watching her as a dot on a stadium screen. South African Amapiano-influenced pop at that venue is going to be a different kind of Sunday night. Tickets are out there now, and this one will sell.
scoring_notes: Tyla skews slightly younger but her crossover appeal is broad. Perimeter's young professional demographic is a solid match. The Roxy is an intimate venue for an artist at her current level of visibility, which is a genuine selling point. Sunday show may limit attendance but that's a minor trade-off.

event_name: Sound of Music Sing-Along at The Strand
blurb: If you've ever hummed Do-Re-Mi while doing something completely unrelated to music, you already know why this is worth your Sunday. The Strand is screening the 1965 Sound of Music as a full sing-along, which means lyrics on screen, everyone participating, and zero judgment when you belt out Edelweiss louder than you planned to. Show up 30 minutes early for a live pre-show concert on the Mighty Allen Theatre Organ, which is a genuinely rare thing to hear in person. At just under three hours it's a full evening, and it's the kind of experience you can't replicate at home on a streaming service. Great for families, great for a date night if your person is the type who knows all the words.
scoring_notes: Sing-along format is a genuinely differentiated experience vs. a standard screening. The live organ pre-show is a rare touch that adds real value. Broad demographic appeal across young families and empty nesters. Marietta is a short drive from the Perimeter coverage zone.

event_name: Jason Bonham's Led Zeppelin Evening at Coca-Cola Roxy
blurb: Here's the thing about Jason Bonham's Led Zeppelin Evening: it's not a tribute band in the traditional sense. Jason is John Bonham's son, he toured with Led Zeppelin himself, and when he plays his father's parts he's playing them from memory, from the inside, the way you can only do when it was your house growing up. If you've got any affinity for Zeppelin's catalog, that context changes what you're watching. The Coca-Cola Roxy is a great room for this kind of show, close enough that you feel it, big enough that it still has energy. Thursday December 10th, 8 PM. Worth a weeknight.
scoring_notes: Led Zeppelin's core fanbase maps well to the 35-55 age range that makes up a significant portion of the Perimeter audience at median age 38. Jason Bonham's specific backstory gives this real uniqueness beyond a standard tribute act. Adult skew fits the newsletter well.

event_name: Chanukah Festival and Menorah Lighting at Vinings Jubilee
blurb: Vinings Jubilee is one of those spots that already feels like a neighborhood gathering place, and on December 6th it gets even better. Chabad of Smyrna is hosting a full Chanukah Festival around the Clocktower starting at 5:30 PM, and it's the kind of evening that works whether you're bringing kids or just want a reason to get outside on a Sunday. There's a menorah lighting, hands-on crafts, face painting, and seasonal treats. Free and open to everyone, no ticket required. RSVP through Chabad of Smyrna is encouraged so they can plan accordingly.
scoring_notes: Vinings sits on the southern edge of the Perimeter coverage area and pulls strongly from that audience. Family-friendly but short enough (2 hours) that it works for adults without kids too. Free price point is a genuine plus here because it lowers the barrier for a Sunday-night outing.

event_name: 6th Annual Dunwoody Village Menorah Lighting & Giant Gelt Drop
blurb: This one is literally in your backyard. The 6th Annual Dunwoody Village Menorah Lighting & Giant Gelt Drop is a full community event put on by Mitzvah House right at Dunwoody Village Pkwy, and it has all the right ingredients for a weeknight that actually feels festive. Rabbi G leads songs, the DHS Band plays, there are donuts and latkes (yes, both), and then the Giant Gelt Drop happens, which, if you've never seen it, is exactly as chaotic and fun as it sounds. The game truck is a nice touch if you're bringing kids. Free, open to everyone, and you don't have to drive far. RSVP ahead so they have a headcount.
scoring_notes: Dunwoody is squarely in the Perimeter coverage zone. Free community event with broad appeal across young families and young professionals. Chanukah timing makes it seasonally unique this week. The Giant Gelt Drop is a genuinely fun hook that differentiates it from a standard menorah lighting.

venue: Sandy Springs Performing Arts Center, Sandy Springs
blurb:
Anastasia is one of those musicals that works on two levels at once. The adults in the room who grew up with the animated film feel it differently than the kids sitting next to them, and both of them walk out happy.

City Springs Theatre Company brings the stage version to Sandy Springs Performing Arts Center starting December 11th. It's a full Broadway-style production from a company that consistently punches above its weight for a suburban venue. Sandy Springs is just east of East Cobb, an easy drive, and the theater itself is a genuinely nice place to spend an evening.

If you've got family in town over the holidays and need something everyone can agree on, this is a strong answer to that problem.
scoring_notes: Strong family fit for East Cobb's mix of established families and empty nesters with college-age or visiting kids. Sandy Springs is accessible from East Cobb. City Springs Theatre is well-regarded in the area. The holiday timing and multigenerational appeal make it relevant for this week's newsletter.

blurb:
The Georgia Symphony Orchestra's Holiday Pops is the kind of thing that feels low-key on paper and then you're sitting there mid-concert realizing this is exactly what you needed in December.

It's festive classics, big orchestral arrangements, sing-alongs if you're into that sort of thing, and Santa shows up at some point, so if you've got younger grandkids or nieces and nephews in town for the holiday, bring them. The Marietta Performing Arts Center is right here in the neighborhood, which means no major traffic, no Battery parking shuffle, just an easy night out.

This is a good one to put on the calendar early so it doesn't sneak past you.
scoring_notes: Marietta MPAC is extremely accessible for East Cobb residents. Family and empty nester appeal is strong. Annual event but well-loved locally and the hyper-local venue is a genuine differentiator from Atlanta events. Good fit for the established families and grandparent-age crowd in this demographic.

venue: Cobb Energy Performing Arts Centre, Atlanta
blurb:
Some holiday traditions stick around because they're actually good. The Nutcracker is one of them.

Atlanta Ballet brings their reimagined production back to Cobb Energy Centre starting December 5th, running through December 26th. The orchestra plays live, which makes a bigger difference than people expect until they're sitting there hearing the Tchaikovsky score fill the room for the first time. This version has been updated with bigger production design and it shows.

If you've got kids still at an age where this feels magical, go. If your kids have aged out of that phase, go anyway, it's a genuinely beautiful show. Cobb Energy is right here, so there's no reason to keep putting this one off every year.
scoring_notes: Annual production but highly relevant to East Cobb's mix of families and empty nesters. The Cobb Energy Centre location is a strong local fit. Live orchestra and updated production add value. Broad age appeal works well for a mixed demographic newsletter.

blurb:
If you have a teenager or a college kid home for the holidays, this is the move.

Tyla hits Coca-Cola Roxy on Sunday, December 6th. The South African singer won a Grammy in 2024 and her sound sits right at the intersection of Afrobeats, R&B, and pop in a way that doesn't feel like any one of those things. If you've heard "Water" and thought you should pay more attention to her, here's your window.

Doors at 8, right in the Battery, so dinner beforehand is easy. Grab your tickets now because this venue sells and her profile has been climbing fast.
scoring_notes: East Cobb has a lot of teens and college-age kids, making this a strong family pick for the holiday weekend. Tyla is genuinely buzzy and this is a one-night show. Some parents in the 40-45 range will also know her work. Skews younger than the typical East Cobb adult event but the family angle makes it relevant.

event_name: Taiwanese Winter Night Market Cooking Class
venue: Mise en Place Cooking Studio, Roswell
blurb:
You've probably scrolled past a hundred recipes for pork belly and never actually made it. Here's your chance to actually learn.

Mise en Place Cooking Studio in Roswell is running a hands-on Taiwanese Night Market class where you'll make braised pork rice bowls, scallion pancakes, Taiwanese cabbage, and pineapple cakes, all in one two-hour session. You're working with other students in small groups, led by a professional chef, and you eat what you make. Wine is included.

This is a genuinely fun date night or a thing to do with a friend you've been meaning to catch up with. Roswell is right down the road, the class is capped at 16 people, and you'll walk out knowing how to make at least three things you'd actually cook again. Worth it.
scoring_notes: Educated, higher-income East Cobb audience with an appetite for food experiences. Roswell location is very accessible from East Cobb. Cooking classes skew well toward the established couples and social-minded adults in this demographic. Unique theme (Taiwanese) differentiates it from generic cooking classes.

blurb:
If you grew up with Led Zeppelin blasting out of a car stereo, this one's going to hit different.

Jason Bonham, son of the legendary John Bonham, brings his Led Zeppelin Evening to Coca-Cola Roxy on December 10th. He's been doing this show for years and the reason people keep coming back is simple: he actually knew these people. He grew up around this music. It's not a cover band cranking out Kashmir for the hundredth time. There's something personal about it that you can feel in the room.

The median age of this audience is 42. That means a lot of you heard your parents play this music, and a decent chunk of you wore out the cassettes yourself. Either way, Coca-Cola Roxy is a great venue and this is a Thursday night worth leaving the house for.
scoring_notes: Strong demographic fit for the 40+ East Cobb audience who grew up with classic rock. Coca-Cola Roxy is close and familiar. Jason Bonham's personal connection to the Zeppelin story elevates this above a standard tribute show. Good fit for couples or groups of friends looking for a weeknight out.

blurb:
This one's been going for 40 years, which tells you everything you need to know about whether people actually show up.

The Marietta Pilgrimage Christmas Home Tour opens five private homes in the Church-Cherokee Historic District, all decorated for the holidays, alongside historic churches and museums in the neighborhood. You're not walking through a staged model home. These are real houses with real history, and the people who open them up take it seriously. Proceeds go to Cobb Landmarks and the Historical Society, so your ticket money stays local.

It runs Friday through Sunday. Grab a friend, make an afternoon of it, and finish somewhere on the Square for dinner after. This is exactly the kind of thing East Cobb was made for.
scoring_notes: Annual event but only comes around once a year and the 40th anniversary adds meaning. Perfect fit for homeowning, historically-minded East Cobb audience. Strong appeal to established families and empty nesters who enjoy local traditions. The community and charitable angle resonates with this demographic.

event_name: Italian Wine Dinner: An Evening with Marchesi Antinori
blurb:
Five courses. Five wines. One of Italy's most storied wine families.

Forno Vero is hosting an intimate dinner built around the Antinori estates, a family that's been making wine in Tuscany since 1385. Each course is designed around a specific wine, taking you from Umbria to Puglia over the course of an evening. This isn't a wine tasting with cheese plates and awkward mingling. It's a real sit-down dinner with food that's actually trying to match what's in your glass.

At $65 a head, this is a STEAL for what's on the table. Spots are limited and this kind of event fills up quietly. Grab your reservation before it disappears.
scoring_notes: High-income, educated East Cobb audience skews heavily toward food and wine experiences. $65 is essentially nothing for a $118K household. The Antinori name carries real weight with wine-aware adults. Intimate format is a strong fit for the established couples and empty nesters in this audience. Genuinely unique, not a recurring weekly thing.

event_name: BLOOPER's Holiday Clubhouse Experience at Truist Park
blurb: This one is genuinely cool, especially if you've got Braves fans in the house over Thanksgiving weekend. BLOOPER's Holiday Clubhouse Experience takes you behind the scenes at Truist Park in a way most fans never get to see: the actual Braves clubhouse, batting cages, dugout access, and the chance to play catch on the field (weather permitting). The whole experience covers up to six guests and includes a holiday photo with BLOOPER Claus, plus a photo op with the 2026 NL East Pennant. If you've got teens who are diehard fans, or if you're just looking for something to do with visiting family that isn't another restaurant reservation, this is the kind of thing people actually remember. It's a Braves-country neighborhood for a reason.
scoring_notes: Truist Park is essentially East Cobb's backyard. Behind-the-scenes access is genuinely rare and can't-miss. Thanksgiving weekend family visit dynamic makes it highly timely. The $118K income demo won't blink at ticket prices. Appeals to teens and adults equally, fitting the older-kids-and-empty-nesters audience well. The 2026 NL East Pennant detail adds a local pride hook.
